    Title:Hunyuan-A13B Technical Report
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:We present Hunyuan-A13B, an open-source large language model based on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture. It contains 80 billion total parameters but activates only 13 billion during inference, balancing model capability, computational efficiency, and deployment cost. The model is pretrained on a rigorously filtered 20T-token corpus with enhanced STEM data curation, improving factual reliability and reasoning ability. High-quality supervised fine-tuning and large-scale reinforcement learning further enhance its overall performance. Hunyuan-A13B also introduces a dual-mode Chain-of-Thought framework that adapts reasoning depth to task complexity: fast thinking for routine queries and slow thinking for complex, multi-step problems. Evaluations show competitive performance across mathematics, science, programming, general language understanding, and agent tasks, often approaching that of much larger models. Its high inference throughput makes it suitable for latency-sensitive applications. We release Hunyuan-A13B to support open research and practical LLM deployment.

report.summary: Tencent's Hunyuan-A13B is an open-source 80B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts LLM that activates only 13B parameters per inference, featuring dual-mode chain-of-thought reasoning and strong efficiency.
report.background: The open-source LLM race has shifted from raw parameter counts toward efficiency, as serving a dense 70B+ model remains prohibitively expensive for most developers. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures solve this by activating only a fraction of weights per token, letting labs scale total capacity while keeping inference cost low. Hunyuan-A13B follows this trend: 80B total parameters but just 13B active, trained on a rigorously filtered 20T-token corpus with extra STEM curation, then refined with supervised fine-tuning and large-scale reinforcement learning. Tencent's release also reflects rising competition among Chinese labs—DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM—to ship capable, permissively licensed models that can run on modest hardware and anchor real production deployments.
key_points: Sparse MoE design: 80B total parameters but only 13B activated per token. This cuts compute and memory bandwidth costs during inference, aiming to give near-large-model quality at a fraction of serving expense, which matters most for latency-sensitive and high-throughput production use.

Training pipeline: a carefully filtered 20T-token corpus with enhanced STEM data, followed by high-quality supervised fine-tuning and large-scale reinforcement learning. Tencent claims this improves factual reliability and reasoning, addressing common complaints about hallucination and weak math/science performance in open models.

Dual-mode chain-of-thought: the model switches between 'fast thinking' for routine queries and 'slow thinking' for multi-step problems. Adaptive reasoning depth avoids wasting tokens on easy prompts while preserving accuracy on hard math, science, and coding tasks.

Evaluation results: competitive performance across mathematics, science, programming, general language understanding, and agent tasks, often approaching much larger models. High inference throughput is highlighted as a key advantage for latency-sensitive applications and cost-conscious deployments.

Open release: weights and technical report are published to support open research and practical LLM deployment, positioning Hunyuan-A13B as a deployable base for fine-tuning, agent building, and enterprise self-hosting.
report.impact: Hunyuan-A13B reinforces the industry's pivot from 'biggest model wins' to 'best efficiency wins.' For the AI industry, it intensifies competition among open-weight MoE models and pressures closed APIs on price-performance. For developers, it offers a stronger option to self-host a capable reasoning model on fewer GPUs, making agentic and STEM-heavy applications more affordable; expect rapid fine-tunes, quantizations, and serving optimizations. For regular users, the practical effects are cheaper AI features, faster responses, and better reasoning in coding assistants and study tools, though benefits depend on how quickly platforms adopt and optimize the weights.
report.tools: To try it: Hugging Face Transformers for loading weights, vLLM and SGLang for high-throughput serving, LMDeploy for optimized inference, and llama.cpp/GGUF or TensorRT-LLM for quantized local deployment. For evaluation, OpenCompass and lm-evaluation-harness are useful; for agents, pair it with LangChain or LlamaIndex. Watch the official Hunyuan GitHub and Hugging Face org for weights, quantization recipes, and updates.
